title: Premium Percentile Base Fee Target
description: Replaces the utilization-based base fee adjustment with a premium-based target to stabilize gas markets and improve tipset efficiency. When the 20th percentile effective premium exceeds 1/8 of the base fee, the base fee increases; when it falls below, the base fee decreases — aligning adjustments with actual congestion signals and reducing proposer transaction duplication.

storageProviders: Storage providers should review gas price configurations (such as premium floors) that may have been tuned for a negligible base fee environment.
Miner software should update default settings to accommodate base fee elasticity — after activation, the base fee will no longer sit near the minimum (100 attoFIL) long-term.

Tipset efficiency is expected to improve: higher base fees reduce priority fee stratification, which in turn reduces transaction duplication among multiple proposers, achieving higher gas utilization.

The proportion of proposer income from premiums will decrease: a higher share of transaction fees will be burned (currently ~99.9% is premium, only ~0.1% burned), though improved utilization from better efficiency may partially offset this.
clients: Because the base fee will rise more often than before, an insufficient gas fee cap may delay message inclusion. Clients should adapt to updated gas estimation recommendations.
Gas pricing will become more predictable — the base fee will genuinely reflect network congestion, allowing users to estimate transaction costs more accurately.
Stuck transactions can be replaced by submitting a new transaction with the same nonce and a higher gas price.
tokenHolders: Higher base fees mean more FIL is burned, directly reducing the network's net inflation rate. Currently ~99.9% of gas fees go to proposers as premium while only ~0.1% is burned; the burn ratio will increase significantly after activation.
Restoring base fee elasticity makes the EIP-1559 economic model work as designed — providing a healthier value support mechanism for FIL.
This proposal does not change the consensus incentive structure but improves the gas market's price signaling function, benefiting network efficiency and long-term ecosystem health.
applicationDevelopers: Dashboards, economic models, and pricing tools that assume current base fee behavior (near-minimum values) will need updates to accommodate base fee elasticity.
Gas price recommendation systems (GasEstimateGasPremium, eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas, eth_gasPrice, GasEstimateFeeCap) should be updated to use mempool-based simulation rather than historical sampling.
The FeeCap estimation formula changes to: FeeCap = Premium + BaseFee * (1 + R)^maxqueueblks, where R = 1/8.
This is a consensus-breaking change — all Filecoin node implementations (Lotus, Forest, Venus) must upgrade. Implementation PRs already exist for Lotus, Forest, and Venus.
